subject: forestSpirit
reasoning:
I'm planning a TypeScript module using only the documented SDK API to build a stylized forest spirit—a bark-skinned humanoid figure about 2 meters tall with antlers, moss, glowing eyes, and blocky stylized primitives, keeping the code concise but visually striking.

I'm mapping out the joint hierarchy, starting with hips as the root, then a catmull spline chain for the spine running up into the chest, making sure to only use sweep, part, joint, and chain functions I'm confident are part of the SDK.

Now I'm extending that hierarchy upward with a neck chain built from two spline points going from the chest to the base of the head, parenting it off the spine chain's final joint.

I won't worry too much about perfect rig correctness here — just keep it sensible. For the arms, I'm setting up limb-like chains: shoulderL near the torso, elbowL bent slightly, and wristL extended outward, with the rest pose having arms out a bit, following the same naming convention as the leg chains.

For legs, I'm defining hipL, kneeL, and ankleL points that curve naturally from hip to foot, parented to the hips, and considering using a limb() helper to place the ankle exactly at a target position with a bend direction.

Three points gives three names total (hipL, kneeL, ankleL), confirming one name per joint point. Now I'm setting up a box geometry for the foot shape.

For hands and head I'm thinking simple spheres and boxes, with the head possibly scaled slightly to be more oval using the scale option on part. I'm leaning toward making the whole figure feel like a forest spirit, with bark-textured body, moss accents, and antlers built from branch-like shapes for the head.

For details I'm planning glowing eyes using a bright emissive-looking color since true emissive materials aren't available, leaf-shaped texture cards scattered across the shoulders and body using surface scattering with randomized placement, and maybe mushroom cap shapes lathed onto the shoulders. For the bark and moss, I'm using grain and mottle paint functions to create wood-grain and mossy patch textures across the torso and legs.

Now I'm figuring out countershading by combining a mossy top paint with a bark-textured bottom paint so the shoulders look mossier while the underside stays barky, then working out antler placement using surface points anchored around the skull with specific azimuth and elevation angles for left and right sides, followed by building the antler shape as a curved path through hit points.

Still defining the antler path...

Adding spikes along antlers, then planning glowing eyes using bright-colored sphere parts on the head.

For the face, I'm thinking a bark-colored sphere for the head with a brow ridge and nose wedge, plus leafy moss cards on top. For the cloak, I'm considering a lathe-based skirt or sweep geometry for a draped leaf-cloak effect.

Sweeping the torso along the spine chain...

For the cloak I'm scattering leaf cards across the torso surface using hit normals to filter placement, then applying textured leaf cards with varied size, lean, and flow direction, picking randomly from multiple leaf textures for variety.

For a bit of extra flair, I'm thinking of adding small lathe-generated mushrooms near the hips or belt, defining a simple stem-and-cap outline as a closed point loop to revolve around the axis.

I want to anchor these to the torso surface using a hit-based placement query to find the right spot and direction, then scatter some small moss-like spheres across the torso for texture.

Deciding against wings or elaborate hair — maybe just a moss beard hanging from the chin using simple cards, kept subtle. For the legs, I'm working out the two-segment limb geometry: checking that hip-to-ankle distances fall within the allowed bend lengths so the knee joint bends forward correctly.

Now I'm laying out the full skeleton chain — hips root, spine curve up through the torso, then a two-segment neck leading to a head joint, making sure each joint gets a unique name and connects to the right parent bone.

For the arms, I'm placing shoulder, elbow, and wrist points slightly angled outward and downward for a natural rest pose, using a smooth catmull curve through those three points per side, mirroring left to right by flipping the x-coordinate, and naming them shoulderL/elbowL/handL (and their mirrored counterparts), all parented to the top of the spine chain.

Adding finger spikes...

For feet, I'm using a box positioned at the ankle joint, offset slightly forward and down to form a simple root-like foot shape.

Adjusting the foot position so it sits flush at ground level, with the ankle offset down 7.5cm giving a bottom at zero. Keeping the foot as a simple box with small toe lumps, then moving on to build the head as a sphere.

For the head joint position, I'm positioning it near the top of the body with the sphere center slightly offset, and considering a squashed scale to make the face shape feel more natural rather than perfectly round. I'm also thinking about adding facial detail through a decal texture positioned on the front of the head.

Writing SVG face code...

I'll skip separate glow eyes since those are already in the SVG, and keep the decal approach simple rather than adding extra sphere eyes. For the overall look I'm sticking with a bark-and-moss woodland palette — browns for the trunk and antlers, greens for moss and leaves, pale cream for antler bone, and a soft glow green accent — while skipping extra flourishes like embers or additional mushroom detail to keep things focused.

Now I'm working out the material shaders: torso uses a countershaded blend of mottled moss tones on top with grainy bark tones below, legs use a simpler vertical bark grain, antlers get a flat bone color, and the mushroom cap gets scattered spot coloring over its base tone. I'm also sketching two leaf textures as small SVGs—one fresh green, one autumn gold—sized to fit as small foliage cards, and considering scattering moss cards across the head surface before deciding that's probably unnecessary detail to skip.

Now I'm designing a moss tuft texture as an SVG with a few curved green strokes radiating upward, sized so the stroke width reads clearly, and planning to scatter these as small cards across the top of the head with a slight lean and downward flow direction. I'm also adding a scattering of leaf cards along the lower and side surfaces of the torso like a cloak, mixing the two leaf textures with some random variation in size, lean, and bend using a seeded random function for natural placement.

For the torso surface I'll use the sweep directly since it's compatible with the surface function. For a hanging skirt around the hips, instead of a lathe (which needs a closed outline), I'm considering a ring of frames placed around a vertical line at the hip height, then scattering leaf cards onto those ring items with a steep lean and downward bend so they read as a draping hem — using the ring's outward-facing frames as anchor points for the hanging leaves.

For antlers, I'm planning to loop over left/right sides and project sprout positions off the head joint's surface (which includes the sphere and decal meshes), then branch tines outward using an along-path approach for each side.

Still defining the sprout call...

For the tines, I'm placing three spikes along the antler's sweep, each using the frame's own axis to determine its direction so they point outward naturally from the sweep surface.

I'm also considering adding a small glowing orb embedded in the chest as a decorative detail stuck onto the torso.

For the back-placed mushroom, I'm figuring out the azimuth near 150 degrees with a slight elevation, using a nearby surface point like [0.14, 1.05, -0.08] to anchor it on the hip/back region.

Writing lathe parameters...

I'll keep just one mushroom for asymmetry plus one at the shoulder, then scatter moss spheres across the torso using a random generator — around 22 small embedded spheres with dark moss coloring to give organic coverage.

Now I'm sorting out imports from the agentic-3js-builder module (createBuilder, rng, catmull, limb, spots, mottle, grain, countershade, svg, line) and starting the actual build code. Writing the setup imports...

Still writing SVG leaf shape... I'm also double-checking that calling svg() at module level versus inside the build function is safe, and deciding to keep these calls inside build to be cautious.

Now I'm setting up the torso texture with a countershaded moss-and-bark pattern, then starting the builder with a hip joint and a spine chain defined through a sequence of catmull-rom control points.

I'm continuing to add the neck chain, head joint with directional orientation, and beginning the torso sweep geometry.

I need to check the round caps on the torso sweep near the hips—the bottom cap radius might make it dip below the hips position, so I should verify that doesn't cause visual overlap.

Now I'm tuning the torso's radius profile along its spine, balancing width at hips versus chest so the silhouette reads as stylized rather than oddly bulging.

Shifting focus to the legs, I'm setting up a loop over left/right sides to build symmetric limbs with root and target points, segment lengths, and a bend direction to shape the knee joint.

Building the chain joints and naming hip, knee, and ankle for each leg, then connecting them to the hips parent. I'm now reasoning through how many names the chain call needs relative to the points and bends, and moving on to sweeping the leg geometry with tapering radii and the coat color.

I'm figuring out the foot placement next, grabbing the ankle joint as the last element of the chain's joint array and positioning a box geometry foot relative to the ankle using local offsets for forward and downward position.

Now I'm setting up the arm chain using a catmull spline for shoulder-elbow-hand joints, parenting it to the spine similar to how the leg chain was structured.

Placing the hand as a small sphere attached directly to the last arm joint, relying on bone-only placement to anchor it at the joint's origin without needing an explicit offset.

For the fingers, I'm figuring out spike positions and directions so they point outward and slightly downward from the hand in a natural splay.

For the head, I'm placing a skull sphere anchored at the head bone, offset slightly upward with a non-uniform scale to give it an elongated shape.

Adding flat shading for a faceted, stylized look, then sketching a nose as a small cone attached to the head, positioned forward and down from center.

Still defining spike parameters... I should explicitly pass bone: head since the spike base point without a bone falls back to the nearest joint, which may not be reliable. Now moving on to the face decal.

I'm skipping extra eye glow details and moving to moss placement: scattering tufts across the skull surface with a normal filter so they only appear on upward-facing areas, then adding card geometry for the moss tufts with leaning and flow direction for a natural growth look.

For the torso, I'm scattering leaf-like cards across the lower, downward-facing surface to create a hanging cloak effect, using lean and bend parameters so the leaves droop outward and downward realistically.

Now I'm adding small moss sphere patches scattered across upward-facing torso areas, and placing a glowing icosahedron at the chest to act as a heart-light detail. I'm also starting to position mushroom shapes at the hip and shoulder using nearest-surface hits as anchor points for lathe-based mushroom geometry...

Writing lathe mushroom code...

Now I'm adding a skirt of leaf-like cards arranged in a ring around the stem, considering whether the ring items naturally face outward for the cards to attach correctly.

Actually better to center the ring at the waist around y=1.02, with the line running from (0,1.02,0) to (0,0.9,0) and the ring radius at 0.2 there. Cards would start at that waist height and lean downward, so I'm checking a leaf card of width 0.13 and length 0.22 leaning at 70 degrees to see where its bottom edge lands relative to the waist.

With a 70-degree lean, the card runs mostly downward, dropping about 0.2 in height so its bottom sits near 0.82 while the leg tops are around 0.95, keeping legs covered by the skirt at radius 0.2. I'm skipping a second skirt layer for simplicity and moving on to finalize the antler tines and wood knot details.

Now I'm writing the SVG markup for the face, using glowing ellipses for eyes, dark brow arcs, and a simple mouth shape within a 64x64 viewBox.

Writing SVG code...

I'm making sure the stroke width scales properly at render size and that the decal's bark background shows through with transparency. Then I move to leaf and tuft SVGs with gold fill colors, and check that the antler's catmull-rom path accepts Hit/Frame values as valid point inputs per the typing system.

I'm working through the sprout function's parameters for antler growth—radius tapering, joint count, and naming conventions that must stay unique per side. For the branch spikes, I'm using the along helper to place smaller spike shapes at intervals, confirming the callback's return value doesn't matter since the part is created as a side effect. Finally I'm checking that the full skeleton has uniquely named joints across hips, spine, limbs, and antlers, and making sure the build function is exported correctly as default.

Writing finger spikes...
